MACBETH (public-domain excerpt from William Shakespeare's Macbeth)

SCENE I. A desert place.
Thunder and lightning. Enter three Witches.
FIRST WITCH. When shall we three meet again?
In thunder, lightning, or in rain?
SECOND WITCH. When the hurlyburly's done,
When the battle's lost and won.
THIRD WITCH. That will be ere the set of sun.
ALL. Fair is foul, and foul is fair:
Hover through the fog and filthy air.

SCENE II. A heath near Forres.
Thunder. Enter the three Witches.
FIRST WITCH. Where hast thou been, sister?
SECOND WITCH. Killing swine.
THIRD WITCH. Sister, where thou?
MACBETH. So foul and fair a day I have not seen.
BANQUO. How far is't called to Forres?
MACBETH. Speak, if you can: what are you?
FIRST WITCH. All hail, Macbeth! hail to thee, thane of Glamis!
BANQUO. Good sir, why do you start; and seem to fear
Things that do sound so fair?

SCENE III. A room in Macbeth's castle. Night.
Enter MACBETH, alone, with a dagger.
MACBETH. Is this a dagger which I see before me,
The handle toward my hand? Come, let me clutch thee.
I see thee still, and on thy blade and dudgeon gouts of blood,
Which was not so before. There's no such thing.
